checked.claim: A Next time of day pressed during an incident before Stage 6 refills every bystander's actions and restocks every room's search tokens (world writes every browser draws), while the bystander's HUD and motive card keep the hour from before the incident.
checked.why: I followed the whole road. The GM panel's advance tile runs boundary.mjs nextTimeOfDay, which refuses only an Eclipse. askReadiness answers go with no round when the primary opens none: roundAllowed is false in an incident before Stage 6, and line 461 returns go at once. nextTimeOfDay then calls advanceTimeOfDay({ resetActions: true }). Nothing in advanceTimeOfDay or applyTimeOfDayChange reads murderState before the refill: the one guard is refilledFor, which is about the boundary and not the incident. Only announceTimeOfDay narrows, and it narrows the card. The panel's button is not disabled in an incident either: advanceHtml disables it for an Eclipse and a Class Trial only. resetActionsFor skips a Monokuma and the published dead only. The refill is trustedWrite on system.resources and flags, and SearchTokens.reset writes the searchTokens world setting, so both reach every client. No reader of the sheet's action row or the room's pips asks clockHiddenHere or clockForDisplay: the files that read either are events, murder, incident-store, hud, rules, eclipse, explain, murder-rules, day-summary, clock, boundary and hud-elapsed. An incident outside an Eclipse is a real state, because openMurder refuses only during an Eclipse and judgePendingMurders opens parked murders after the flag clears. The comment at clock.mjs:889-890 records the refill as known ('happened either way'). It is not an owner's decision about the refill, and the motive card was later held for the same kind of tell (events.mjs:91-97), so it does not refute the finding.

checked.claim: endTimedEffect drops a row in finally even when its take throws, which leaves the bonus on the sheet for good, and the uncaught throw stops endTimedEffects or endAtEclipseStart mid-loop, so keepEndedAtStart is skipped.
checked.why: The control flow is as written: the take runs in try, the row is dropped in finally, there is no catch, and the loops in endTimedEffects (225), endEclipseEffects (113) and endAtEclipseStart (362) call it bare. keepEndedAtStart at 365 runs only after that loop. What I could not find is anything that makes take throw on this road. trustedWrite is stampOf, then noteOwnWrite, then doc.update. stampOf throws only for a reason outside WRITE_REASONS, and 'facility' is in the list (resource-guard.mjs:268). The writer is the primary GM, who may write any actor. A preUpdate hook's false makes update resolve with nothing, not reject. A trait taken below zero is measured to write (-2, timed-effects.mjs:20-22), so validation is not a trigger. A missing actor skips the take (206), and an Experience take returns early when its entry is gone (79). forcedDeletion() exists on v14. The failure scenario ('a sheet write refused or the connection drops') names two triggers. The first does not throw. The second was not shown to reject an awaited update. The defect is real robustness dirt, but its scenario rests on a throw nobody has shown, so it does not reach 'wrong in a particular situation'.

checked.claim: Renaming a room's flat table in Item tables repoints the rooms' drpgItemTable flag but leaves '<old> - Tier N' and '<old> - <plural>' on the old base, so no draw reads them.
checked.why: Rename (tables-editor.mjs:1225-1248) runs current().update({ name }), then repointRooms and the pane's own text, and does nothing else. repointRooms walks regions whose table flag equals the old name and calls setVaultRoom with the new name. A room's draw base is that flag (vault-store.mjs:578-580 roomTable, which tables-pools.mjs:995 reads through tableForRoom). drawRoomNamed builds '<base> - Tier N', '<base> - <plural>' and '<base>', and finds each by getName. drawRoomAny keeps a table only when isRoomTableOf(base, name) holds, and that needs the name to start with '<base> - '. Nothing links a split table to its room except its name. I looked for another road: the RollTable hooks in tables-pools.mjs (1155-1157) only clear the name index, and no updateRollTable listener renames a family (grep of scripts/). clearSplitPiece is about a region's pieces, not tables. The tier-2 test that names the rename (tests-tier2.mjs:67927) uses a flat table with no split tables, so it pins nothing opposite.

checked.claim: boostUltimate run on a GM that is not the primary drops the ultimateBoost row but tells no owner (tellOwners is primary-only), so the player's sheet keeps the 'stronger Ultimate' badge.
checked.why: The road: a GM buying a Hope Call on a student's sheet takes calls.mjs's GM branch, where gmPays is false and the Hope is paid locally. applyCall calls call-effects.mjs armCall, whose GM branch calls appendArmedCall on that GM's browser. requestArmCall's local road does the same for a GM asker (bridge-asks.mjs:466-477). appendArmedCall calls boostUltimate for key 'ultimate' on any GM. boostUltimate checks only game.user.isGM, writes the list and calls tellOwners, which returns unless isPrimaryGm(). Other roads I looked for: the store row has afterRestore only (gm-stores.mjs:1091-1096), and its own doc says 'Written, read and dropped by the primary alone', which boostUltimate breaks. The gm-store engine has no hook that resends a copy on a merge (its Hooks.on are userConnected, clientSettingChanged and the setting hooks at 1746-1754), and defineCopy's receive is called only from timed-effects.mjs's socket. The owner's copy is sent on tellOwners, the owner's ask at ready or drpgPrimaryReady, and retellTimedEffects. live.mjs hearing the copy by key does not help, because the copy itself is not changed. The sheet's badges read the copy (rowsHere, effectBadges), so a re-render of the sheet for the pendingCall flag still draws the old row. E93-T13 arms on the primary only.

checked.claim: Add an item has no way to add an entry to room pools only while its tier pool exists; the comment promises a '-' choice.
checked.why: The tier select is built from ITEM_TIERS alone (tables-editor.mjs:940-942) with no '-' option. readNewItemForm always puts tierTableIdFor(category, tier) first, so the comment at 1636-1640 does not match the code. But Add is not dead: it adds the entry and says which tier pool it goes into (paintTierTarget, 1129-1140). This is a missing choice and a comment against the code, not a control that does nothing. The reader filed it as a hint with no severity, and it belongs under comments_against_code or ux at nit.
